citation.sourceDocument: IRS Education Credits (Form 8863); IRC §25A (AOTC & Lifetime Learning Credit)
citation.sourceNote: Two credits, one set of expenses, and you may not claim both for the same student in the same year — which is the whole point of the comparison tile. The American Opportunity Tax Credit (IRC §25A(i)) is 100% of the first $2,000 of qualified expenses plus 25% of the next $2,000, so $2,500 maximum, and 40% of it is REFUNDABLE — up to $1,000 back even with no tax liability. It is limited to four tax years per student, requires at least half-time enrollment in a degree program, and is barred by a felony drug conviction. The Lifetime Learning Credit (§25A(c)) is 20% of up to $10,000 of expenses, so $2,000 maximum, entirely NONREFUNDABLE — but it has no year limit, no enrollment-level requirement, and is per RETURN rather than per student, which makes it the better credit for a part-time student, a graduate student, or someone taking a single course. Both phase out between $80,000 and $90,000 of modified AGI ($160,000 to $180,000 joint); those thresholds are statutory and have not been indexed since the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021 aligned the Lifetime Learning Credit to the AOTC's range. Married filing separately may claim neither. Omitted: the coordination with §529 distributions and tax-free scholarships (which reduce qualified expenses), the qualified-expense definition itself (tuition and required fees, plus course materials for the AOTC only — never room and board), and the tuition-and-fees deduction, which was repealed. Verified against IRC §25A and the IRS Education Credits (AOTC and LLC) page on 2026-08-29.
